findings.title: sd18_*_widening.rs (89 files) and sd13_*progression*.rs (95 files) are a near-byte-identical template varying only per-level numbers -- 184 of 543 files (33.9%), 79,750 of 187,008 lines (42.6%)
findings.evidence: `diff tests/sd18_barbarian_level12_widening.rs tests/sd18_barbarian_level13_widening.rs` shows the doc comment, imports, both helper fns (`load`, `explanation`), and all 8 test-fn skeletons are structurally identical between adjacent levels -- only numeric expectations and prose numbers change (confirmed exemplar-by-exemplar against tests/sd18_fighter_level16_widening.rs, a different class, same 5-shape idiom: base-attack-and-saves / feature-genuinely-rises / remaining-pillars-carry-over / negative-controls x3 / matrix-row-assertion). sd18_*_widening.rs: 89 of 117 sd18 files, 37,726 lines. sd13_*progression*.rs: 95 of 175 sd13 files, 42,024 lines. Both families cover the same 11 classes (barbarian/bard/cleric/druid/fighter/monk/paladin/ranger/rogue/sorcerer/wizard) at different level ranges (sd13 ~1-11, sd18 ~11-20). Repo-wide totals: 543 files, 187,008 lines.
findings.fix_description: CONSOLIDATION PROPOSAL (table-driven, coverage-identical). (1) Add tests/common/mod.rs (a subdirectory module, not a top-level test binary, so it costs 0 extra binaries) holding the shared `load()`/`explanation()`/`has_explanation()`/`claim_blocking()` helpers (see R10-F2) plus a `macro_rules! class_level_widening_test!` that takes {level, prior_fixture_const, this_fixture_const, expected: struct-literal of per-level numeric fields, carries_over: slice of (id,val) pairs, rises: slice of (id,val,prior_val) pairs, negative_control_levels} and expands to the SAME set of named #[test] fns the hand-written files already use (e.g. `barbarian_level12_base_attack_and_saves_genuinely_rise`) -- so `cargo test <name>` and any CI history keyed on test names keeps working unchanged. (2) One new file per class per family (e.g. tests/sd18_barbarian_widening.rs invoking the macro once per level 12..20; tests/sd13_barbarian_progression.rs once per level 2..11) replaces that class's per-level files. Binaries: 11 classes x 2 families = 22 files replace 184 -> repo-wide 543 -> 381 binaries (543-184+22); a more aggressive same-class-both-families merge (11 files total) would reach 543 -> 370, at the cost of mixing two loop-generations' file-naming history in one file -- recommend the conservative 22-file/381-binary option first. (3) Compile/link-time win is NOT measured here (read-only mandate) -- the claim rests on the well-known fact that each tests/*.rs top-level file is a SEPARATE crate compile+link+process-spawn unit; removing 162 of them (184-22) removes 162 separate link steps and process spawns from `cargo test`'s tail, independent of and additive to any parallelism gain. (4) Estimated line delta: per-exemplar breakdown of tests/sd18_barbarian_level12_widening.rs (377 lines) is ~43 lines doc-comment + ~27 lines helpers + ~279 lines across 8 test fns; folding the 27 duplicated helper lines into tests/common (one-time cost, amortized across 314 files, see R10-F2) and collapsing each level's ~279 lines of hand-written test-fn bodies into one macro invocation (~40-70 lines: a struct literal of expected values plus a short doc-comment carrying the primary-source citation, which the migration must PRESERVE, not delete, since it is this repo's own audit trail of independently-checked CRB rule text) yields roughly 60-70 lines per level. Projected total: sd18 89 files x ~65 lines = ~5,785 lines; sd13 95 files x ~65 lines = ~6,175 lines; + one shared macro definition (~400-600 lines, written once). New total ~12,500 lines vs current 79,750 -- an estimated 84% reduction (~67,000 lines removed), unverified without actually building it. (5) MIGRATION PATH keeping coverage identical: for one class at a time -- (a) write the new per-class file using the macro against the SAME fixture files (fixtures/rules_core/*.txt are untouched); (b) run `cargo test --no-run -- --list` (or equivalent) on the old per-level files' union and on the new file, diff the two SORTED test-name lists and require byte-for-byte equality before deleting any old file; (c) only after that equality check passes, delete the old per-level files for that class; (d) repeat class-by-class so a single class's migration failure never blocks the others. Because this rewrites files inside the two explicitly-excluded 'templated test families', and because I cannot run cargo in this read-only lane, this stays report_only regardless of how mechanical it looks.
findings.risk_notes: The doc-comment prose in each file is a real audit trail (primary-source citations, cross-references to sibling files, notes on which negative-control boundary moved and why) -- a naive mechanical strip-to-macro would destroy that grounding history; the migration must carry it forward per-row, not delete it. Any consolidation must preserve the exact #[test] function names (used for `cargo test <name>` and any historical CI dashboards keyed on test name) -- do not rename during the same change that merges files.

findings.title: 312 of 543 files (57.5%) hand-copy a byte-identical `fn load()` helper; 265 of 271 files with `explanation()` and 116 of 119 files with `has_explanation()` are also byte-identical -- a tests/common module was never introduced
findings.evidence: Programmatic AST-free scan (regex + brace-matching over all 543 tests/*.rs) found: `fn load(fixture: &str) -> CharacterInput { ... }` appears in 314 files, 312 of which are textually identical (whitespace-normalized) to the body at tests/sd18_barbarian_level12_widening.rs:71-81; `fn explanation<'a>(...)` appears in 271 files, 265 identical to tests/sd18_barbarian_level12_widening.rs:83-97; `fn has_explanation(...)` appears in 119 files, 116 identical. Breaking the 314 `load()`-defining files down by prefix: 170 sd13, 116 sd18, 7 ge06, 6 sd24, 5 v06, 4 sd21, 1 each of wizard/sorcerer/sd49/sd27/sd25/hybrid -- i.e. 28 of the 314 files (8.9%) sit OUTSIDE the two named templated families, proving the duplication is a repo-wide test-infrastructure gap, not something scoped only to sd13/sd18.
findings.fix_description: Add tests/common/mod.rs (Cargo's documented idiom: a tests/<name>/mod.rs path is NOT auto-discovered as its own test binary, so this costs zero additional compiled binaries) exporting `pub fn load(fixture: &str) -> CharacterInput`, `pub fn explanation<'a>(...)`, `pub fn has_explanation(...)`, and `pub fn claim_blocking(...)` (21 files share this one too). Each of the up to 314 consuming files adds `mod common; use common::*;` and deletes its own copy. This is independent of and complementary to R10-F1's macro consolidation -- it should land FIRST since it benefits the 28 non-templated-family files immediately and de-risks F1 by giving the new per-class macro files a shared base to build on.
findings.risk_notes: A handful of files use signature variants (fully-qualified `codex::rules_core::...` return types, or operate on `PilotViewModel`/`PilotHeadlessReceipt` instead of `PilotBaseChassisComputation`) -- these must NOT be force-migrated to the common signature; verify each file's variant before switching it to `use common::*;` (per this repo's own 'a field name is not its meaning' / corpus-identifier-scope-collision lessons: same fn name, different contract).

findings.title: 28 of 68 #[test] fns across 16 files gate their only real-corpus assertions behind a bare `CORPUS_ROOT` env var with no fallback -- a sibling `PCGEN_CORPUS_ROOT` convention (26 other files) defaults to $HOME and actually finds the corpus on this box, so the two conventions silently diverge and scripts/verify.sh sets neither
findings.evidence: tests/sd19_school_evocation.rs:35-43 defines `fn corpus_root() -> Option<PathBuf> { match std::env::var("CORPUS_ROOT") { Ok(v) => ...Some/None, Err(_) => None } }` -- no fallback path. Its test at :79-109 (`evocation_school_spell_count_matches_real_corpus`) does `let Some(root) = corpus_root() else { eprintln!("...skipping..."); return; }` BEFORE any assert executes -- i.e. it passes with zero assertions run whenever `CORPUS_ROOT` (that exact name) is unset. 16 files share this exact bare-`CORPUS_ROOT`-no-fallback pattern (all sd19_school_*.rs [8], sd19_equipment_*.rs [4], sd19_feat_catalog.rs, sd17_b_spells.rs, v06_apg_acg_feat_catalog.rs, sd19_seam_shapes_correctness.rs is NOT in this set -- it uses the other variant), containing 68 #[test] fns total, 28 of which contain this exact `let Some(root) = corpus_root() else { ...; return; }` skip-gate. Meanwhile a DIFFERENT, larger cluster of 26 files (sd17_b_races_and_abilities.rs, sd17_b5_equipment.rs, all sd22_*_resolves.rs, sd27_feat_prerequisite_enforcement.rs, sd31_e2_ground_truth_agreement.rs, the derived_evaluator_fixture_check_* family, etc.) instead check `PCGEN_CORPUS_ROOT` with a fallback to `$HOME/workspace/repos/pcgen/data` -- which resolves successfully on this box (confirmed: `~/workspace/repos/pcgen/data` exists and is populated). `grep -n 'CORPUS_ROOT' scripts/verify.sh` returns zero lines that export or set either variable -- verify.sh relies entirely on ambient environment. So a maintainer who has only ever exported `PCGEN_CORPUS_ROOT` (or relies on its $HOME default, which just works) gets full real-corpus verification for the 26-file cluster but ZERO verification -- no error, no visible red, just a quiet eprintln -- for the entire sd19 school/equipment cluster's 28 corpus-parity tests, with nothing distinguishing 'intentionally skipped' from 'gate satisfied' in a normal test-run summary.
findings.fix_description: Rename the bare `CORPUS_ROOT` check in the 16-file cluster to `PCGEN_CORPUS_ROOT` with the same $HOME-fallback the 26-file cluster already uses (or, better, move both variants into the shared tests/common module from R10-F2 so there is exactly one corpus-discovery function repo-wide). This directly closes this repo's own standing hazard: 'a gate that cannot fail proves nothing' -- these 28 tests currently cannot fail in any environment that only sets the other variable name.
findings.risk_notes: Before renaming, confirm none of the 16 files intentionally want a narrower/different corpus root than the PCGen-data default (e.g. a curated subset) -- read each file's surrounding doc comment first; a couple of these files may have chosen `CORPUS_ROOT` deliberately to mean something distinct from `PCGEN_CORPUS_ROOT`, though no such distinction was found in the ones inspected.

findings.title: 28 of 543 files (5.2%) contain #[ignore]-tagged tests that scripts/verify.sh never runs at all -- no `--include-ignored` or `-- --ignored` anywhere in the script
findings.evidence: `grep -l '#\[ignore' tests/*.rs` returns 28 files (sd17_a_include_graph.rs, sd17_b1_martial_class.rs, sd17_b_monster_stat_block.rs, sd17_b_spellcasting_class.rs, all 18 sd22_*_resolves.rs files, sd27_feat_prerequisite_enforcement.rs, sd31_e2_ground_truth_agreement.rs, pcgen_runner_smoke.rs, v06_work_inventory.rs), each with `#[ignore = "requires a local PCGen corpus checkout; set PCGEN_CORPUS_ROOT=/path/to/pcgen/data"]` immediately above the `#[test]` (e.g. tests/sd17_b1_martial_class.rs:513-514). `grep -n 'ignored\|include-ignored' scripts/verify.sh` returns nothing, and every `cargo test` invocation in scripts/verify.sh (lines 1234, 1298, 1341, 1368) is a plain `cargo test --locked ...` with no ignored-test flag. Rust's `cargo test` never runs `#[ignore]`-tagged tests by default, so these tests are entirely absent from every scripts/verify.sh run -- distinct from R10-F3's tests, which at least print an eprintln when skipped; these produce no output at all.
findings.fix_description: Either (a) add a dedicated `--include-ignored` stage to scripts/verify.sh gated on the same corpus-presence check the tests themselves use (so it runs for real when the corpus is checked out, e.g. in a nightly/manual lane, and is visibly skipped as a whole stage otherwise), or (b) if these are meant to stay permanently opt-in/manual, add a one-line comment at the top of scripts/verify.sh noting that 28 files' worth of corpus-grounding tests are intentionally excluded from the standard gate and must be run manually with `cargo test -- --ignored`, so a future auditor does not mistake 'no visible mention' for 'not present'.
findings.risk_notes: This may be an intentional trade-off (these tests need a large external PCGen checkout not everyone has) rather than an oversight -- verdict is PLAUSIBLE, not CONFIRMED, since I cannot know the original authors' intent; treat as a documentation/discoverability gap rather than a correctness defect.

findings.title: `corpus_root()` is reused as a function name for at least 3 semantically different contracts across the corpus-touching test files (Option<PathBuf> from an env var vs. a fixed repo-relative PathBuf), inviting a copy-paste-the-wrong-variant mistake
findings.evidence: Across the 26+16=~40 files that define a `corpus_root`-shaped helper, 8 distinct function bodies exist under the SAME name: (1) 16 files: `fn corpus_root() -> Option<PathBuf>` reading env `CORPUS_ROOT`, no fallback (R10-F3's cluster); (2) 2 files (sd17_b5_equipment.rs and one other): `fn corpus_root() -> Option<PathBuf>` reading `PCGEN_CORPUS_ROOT` with a `$HOME` fallback; (3) ~24 more files: a close variant of (2) with minor formatting/ordering differences; (4) tests/sd27_license_stripping_shape_v1.rs:51-53 and tests/sd29_declared_product_identity_in_shipped_race_traits.rs: `fn corpus_root() -> PathBuf` (non-Optional, infallible) returning `env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR").join("data/corpus")` -- this is a REPO-VENDORED generated corpus, not the external PCGen raw-source checkout the other two families reference. A future edit that copy-pastes a `corpus_root()` call from one file into another without checking which of the two totally different corpora (external PCGen `.lst` source vs. repo-vendored `data/corpus` JSON cache) it resolves to would silently point at the wrong data set and still compile.
findings.fix_description: Rename the repo-vendored variant to `generated_corpus_root()` (or similar) to make the two concepts textually distinct, and fold the external-PCGen variants into the single shared helper proposed in R10-F2/R10-F3.
findings.risk_notes: Low-severity naming hygiene issue; no evidence found in this pass of an actual mix-up having occurred, only that the shared name makes one easy to introduce.

cross_chunk: R10-F1 and R10-F2 are the same root cause at two scopes: F1 is the templated-family-specific test-BODY duplication (79,750 of 187,008 lines, 42.6%); F2 is the repo-wide helper-FUNCTION duplication (up to 314 of 543 files, 57.8%) that F1's macro consolidation should build on top of rather than duplicate. Any lane doing housekeeping on tests/ should sequence F2 (introduce tests/common) before F1 (introduce per-class macros).

R10-F3 and R10-F4 are two DIFFERENT shapes of the same standing lesson ('a gate that cannot fail proves nothing'): F3 is a silent-pass-with-eprintln pattern reachable under normal `cargo test`, F4 is a compile-time-visible-but-never-scheduled pattern (#[ignore]) that scripts/verify.sh never opts into. Neither is caught by the other's fix.

No lane in this review should treat tests/sd18_*_widening.rs or tests/sd13_*progression*.rs files as auto_fix candidates even for the load()/explanation() dedup piece of R10-F2, per the explicit templated-test-family exclusion in this review's ground rules -- 28 of the 314 affected files fall outside that exclusion (see R10-F2 evidence) and could be handled independently if another lane wants a smaller, immediately actionable slice.
lane_summary.notes: Scope per the dispatch: tests/ only, 543 top-level .rs integration-test binaries, 187,008 total lines, 0 files matched a 'GENERATED FILE' marker (checked by reading, not filename, across the full 543). (a) Read 4 exemplars in full (tests/sd18_barbarian_level12_widening.rs, tests/sd18_barbarian_level13_widening.rs, tests/sd13_barbarian_level3_progression.rs, plus a partial read of tests/sd18_fighter_level16_widening.rs for a third class) and diffed two adjacent-level pairs (sd18 barbarian 12/13, sd13 barbarian 3/4); confirmed via `wc -l`/`ls` that sd18_*_widening.rs = 89 of 117 sd18 files (37,726 lines) and sd13_*progression*.rs = 95 of 175 sd13 files (42,024 lines), matching the dispatch's ~184-file/~80k-line estimate. (b) Full prefix-family binary census (denominators against the 543 total) is in R10-F1's evidence and reproduced here: sd13 175, sd18 117, sd20 57, sd22 30, sd27 29, v06 18, sd19 16, sd24 15, sd17 11, sd26 10, derived 10, sd25 9, ge06 9, sd31 4, sd21 4, pi 3, ge08 3, character 2, and 19 further one-off-prefix files (wizard/spell/sorcerer/sd49/sd30/sd29/sd28/sd14/sd/saved/pcgen/pcc/no/hybrid/golden/generator/ge05/formula/feat/equipment/duergar), summing to 543. No compile or link timing was measured (mandate: measure nothing); F1's compile-time claim is qualitative (fewer separate compile+link+process-spawn units), not a benchmark. (c) Sampled the remaining ~359-file population (543-89-95) across 13+ distinct prefix clusters (sd20, sd22, sd27, v06, sd19, sd24, sd17, sd26, sd25, derived, ge06, sd21, sd31 -- one to three files read/measured per cluster) plus a repo-wide programmatic scan (regex + brace-matching, not full AST) for the `load`/`explanation`/`has_explanation`/`claim_blocking`/`corpus_root` helper-duplication clusters described in F2/F3/F5. (d) Checked systematically for vacuous tests: a Python brace-matching scan over all 4,597 `#[test]` fns in the 543 files found ZERO test bodies lacking an `assert`/`panic!`/`unwrap()`/`expect(`/`should_panic` call -- no purely-vacuous test bodies exist in this codebase. Also checked for `assert!(true)`, `assert_eq!(1,1)`-shaped tautologies (0 found), `.len() >= 0` / unsigned-always-true comparisons (0 found), and commented-out assert lines (19 grep hits, all false positives -- prose mentioning the word 'assert', not disabled code, one of which -- tests/sd24_acg_class_coverage_audit.rs:472-485 -- is itself a well-designed anti-vacuity guard worth noting as a positive pattern, not a finding). The real 'gate that cannot fail' hazard in this codebase is NOT literal vacuous-test-body syntax but the early-return-on-missing-env-var pattern documented in R10-F3 (28 of 68 tests across 16 files) and the never-scheduled #[ignore] pattern in R10-F4 (28 files).
